# HLT-C12 eligibility proposal (A2, candidate)

Study: Sweeney, A., Fahmy, S., Nolan, F., et al. (2014). The relationship between therapeutic alliance and service user satisfaction in mental health inpatient wards and crisis house alternatives: A cross-sectional study. PLOS ONE, 9(7), e100153.

Proposal: eligible.

## Criterion 1: relationship in a public or publicly funded service
- The object is the therapeutic alliance between staff and service users in 16 acute inpatient wards of two NHS Trusts and four crisis houses in the same inner London catchment areas (p.2, Study design and setting).
- Crisis houses range from statutory-sector services to voluntary-sector services; all are "closely linked into the local catchment area acute service systems, with crisis resolution teams the primary referrers to both wards and crisis houses" (p.2).
- Funding of the study: NIHR, HS&DR programme (p.1).
- Point to check: the text does not state explicitly that the voluntary-sector crisis houses are publicly commissioned; NHS referral routes and integration in the acute system point to publicly funded provision.

## Criterion 2: at least one qualitative and one quantitative finding
- Quantitative: structured interviews with 355 service users (108 crisis house, 247 ward); STAR-P, CSQ, IPR, RAS, NES-S/NES-P; adjusted linear regressions (p.2-4, Tables 1-5).
- Qualitative: semi-structured interviews with 29 service users and 13 staff in four crisis houses and five wards, thematic analysis (p.3, p.4-10, Table 6).

Both criteria are met. Joint claims were not used as a criterion.
